name: Sikh Empire
summary: A Punjabi state founded by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Its religiously mixed court and modernised Khalsa army made it the last major Indian power to fall to the British.

location.value: The Punjab, Kashmir and the Peshawar valley; capital Lahore (from 1802).

terrain.value: The five rivers of the Punjab plain, rising to the Himalaya and the Khyber Pass.
terrain.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

climate.value: Hot summers, monsoon rains and cold winters.
climate.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

resources.value: Fertile irrigated farmland, Kashmir shawl wool, salt mines.
resources.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

disasters.value: No major disasters are recorded in the sources checked.
disasters.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

population.value: About 12 million (1800s, infobox); other contemporary estimates range from 3.5 to 15 million.

urbanisation.value: Lahore and Amritsar were the main cities.
urbanisation.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

disease.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

migration.value: Soldiers and officers came from many regions, including European officers.
migration.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

economicBase.value: Land revenue from farming, reportedly around 70% of state income.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade between India, Afghanistan and Central Asia; Kashmir shawls exported.
tradeRoutes.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

moneyAndTax.value: Nanakshahi coins (silver rupees with Persian legends).

inequality.value: Landowners and military chiefs (sardars) held much wealth.
inequality.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

governmentType.value: Federal monarchy under a maharaja; court known as the Lahore Darbar.

keyRulers.value: Ranjit Singh (1801–1839), Kharak Singh, Sher Singh, regent Jind Kaur, Duleep Singh (last).

succession.value: Chaotic after Ranjit Singh: several rulers were killed within six years.
succession.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

institutions.value: A centralised army and revenue system with officials of all religions.
institutions.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

stability.value: Court murders and factional struggle after 1839.
stability.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

eliteConflict.value: Rival court factions (the Dogra brothers, the Sandhawalias) and an assertive army.
eliteConflict.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

armyAndTech.value: The Khalsa army, trained in European style with modern artillery, was one of the strongest in Asia.
armyAndTech.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

majorWars.value: Afghan–Sikh Wars; Sino-Sikh War (1841–42); First and Second Anglo-Sikh Wars (1845–46, 1848–49).

territoryChange.value: About 520,000 km² in 1839; took Multan (1818), Kashmir (1819) and Peshawar.

alliancesRivals.value: Treaty of Amritsar with the British (1809); rivals: the Durrani Afghans, later the British.
alliancesRivals.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

inventions.value: Adopted European military drill and artillery.
inventions.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

scienceEducation.value: Persian-language administration; gurdwara and mosque schools.
scienceEducation.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

openness.value: Hired French, Italian and other European officers.
openness.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

religion.value: Sikhism was the ruling faith, with a Muslim majority and a Hindu minority.

languageWriting.value: Persian (court); Punjabi, Kashmiri, Pashto and Dogri widely spoken.

artsArchitecture.value: The gilding of the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) under Ranjit Singh; Sikh miniature painting.
artsArchitecture.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

socialStructure.value: Maharaja, sardars, soldiers, peasants of all faiths.
socialStructure.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

sharedIdentity.value: Motto “Akal Sahai” (“With God’s Grace”); Sikh Khalsa traditions.

neighbours.value: The British East India Company, Afghanistan, Tibet, Nepal.

ideasReligions.value: Sikh institutions spread across the Punjab.
ideasReligions.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

riseSignals.value: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore in 1799 and was crowned in 1801.

peakPeriod.value: At Ranjit Singh’s death, with the empire at its largest.

declineSignals.value: Succession murders and a powerful, restless army.
declineSignals.source: Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (1990)

outcome.value: Annexed after the Second Anglo-Sikh War; became British Punjab.

sources.value: Persian court records and British accounts. Checked against Wikipedia (“Sikh Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Population and religious-share figures vary widely.

knownFor.label: Gilded Golden Temple
knownFor.note: Ranjit Singh covered the Harmandir Sahib in gold leaf.

knownFor.label: Khalsa army
knownFor.note: A European-trained army that fought the British to a standstill in several battles.

knownFor.label: Koh-i-Noor diamond
knownFor.note: Taken by Ranjit Singh from Shah Shuja; passed to Britain in 1849.

knownFor.label: Kashmir shawls
knownFor.note: Fine wool shawls exported to Europe.
